title: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0, a stable base for running AI models locally

sources.name: RIO Rundown (Substack) daily AI news roundup

kept.claim: From now on, both llama.cpp and ggml will signal API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps.
kept.evidence: Source 0: 'both llama.cpp and ggml will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps'. Source 1: major-version bumps will now reflect API and ABI incompatibilities, to ensure stability for downstream consumers.

kept.claim: llama.cpp runs multi-modal LLMs across a wide range of hardware, from consumer machines to enterprise servers, using quantization, optimized backends and a portable C/C++ implementation.
kept.evidence: Source 0 intro, which says the same thing in these terms. Source 1 Spotlight: 'Through quantization and optimized backends, the C/C++ implementation enables multi-modal LLM inference across hardware'.

kept.claim: Hardware support from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel is used to add self-hosted CI runners across major hardware platforms. The roundup words this more loosely, as 'hardware support'.
kept.evidence: Source 0: 'With hardware support from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel, we continue to enroll more self-hosted runners'. Source 1 key point: 'Hardware support includes NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, and Intel.'

kept.claim: CI infrastructure is being expanded to check correctness of every change that lands on the master branches. The post credits Hugging Face's HF Buckets and HF Jobs for the scaling.
kept.evidence: Source 0: HF Buckets and HF Jobs let them 'guarantee correctness for every change that lands on the master branches'. Source 1: CI improvements ensure correctness for changes on master branches. Only source 0 names HF Buckets and HF Jobs.

dropped.claim: The ggml-org team announced llama.cpp v1.0.0 on November 13, 2026, one day before the RIO Rundown roundup of Nov 14, 2026.
dropped.evidence: The Hugging Face post is marked 'Published November 13, 2026' and says 'Today we release libraries v1.0.0'. The roundup is dated Nov 14, 2026 and only repeats the news.

dropped.claim: The v1.0.0 releases cover two libraries: llama.cpp (libllama) and ggml (libggml).
dropped.evidence: The blog's Releases table lists 'llama.cpp v1.0.0' (libllama) and 'ggml v1.0.0' (libggml). The roundup mentions only llama.cpp.

dropped.claim: The roundup says v1.0.0 'provides a stable API and ABI for downstream consumers'. The primary post does not say this outright. It commits to marking breaking changes with major-version bumps and says a stable API is paramount.
dropped.evidence: Source 1 key point: 'llama.cpp v1.0.0 provides a stable API and ABI for downstream consumers.' Source 0 only describes the versioning policy going forward.

dropped.claim: Semantic versioning rules for all ggml-org projects: MAJOR = breaking change to the public C API in ./include; MINOR = backward-compatible feature, backend updates, model support, or API addition; PATCH = bug fix with no API change.
The project is about 3.5 years old and many downstream applications already depend on it.
dropped.evidence: Source 0: 'During the 3.5 years since its inception... many downstream applications already depend on our work'.

dropped.claim: llama.cpp currently supports more than 150 architecture variants, plus all mainstream speculative decoding methods.
dropped.evidence: Source 0: 'supports more than 150 architecture variants as well as all mainstream speculative decoding methods'.

dropped.claim: Distribution channels listed: pre-release artifacts (Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS), Docker (Linux), Debian (Linux), Homebrew (macOS, Linux), conda-forge (Windows, macOS, Linux), MacPorts (macOS), Winget (Windows), XCFramework (iOS, macOS).
The post points readers to Llama desktop apps for MacOS and Windows, shipped by the team behind llama.cpp and Hugging Face.

Verification gap: no second independent original report was read. The GitHub release pages for llama.cpp and ggml v1.0.0 returned only page metadata in my fetch, and the follow-up fetch and web search were blocked by the tool-use limit. Every claim above therefore rests on the primary post plus, at most, a roundup that summarizes it. Claims supported only by source 0 are unconfirmed by a second source.
dropped.evidence: The roundup's llama.cpp item links directly to source 0 as its 'Read More' and adds no independent reporting.
